record.paper_title: Some open problems on the analysis of the Cauchy-Fueter system in several variables
record.context_brief: Several variables as one hypercomplex variable
record.original_question: Given a hypercomplex algebra A and a notion of A-regularity, find a hypercomplex algebra C and a corresponding notion of C-regularity such that every A-regular function of several variables appears as a special case of a C-regular function of one variable. The motivating examples are that regular functions of two quaternionic variables can be viewed as regular functions of one biquaternionic variable or one suitable Clifford variable.

evidence.quote: Problem: Given an hypercomplex algebra A and the notion of A-regularity, find a hypercomplex algebra C and a corresponding notion of C-regularity.
regular functions in two quaternionic variables can be seen as regular functions of one biquaternionic variable.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $A$ be a finite-dimensional real hypercomplex algebra (i.e., a unital associative real algebra generated by a finite set of "imaginary" units, such as the quaternions $\mathbb{H}$, the biquaternions $\mathbb{H}\otimes_{\mathbb{R}}\mathbb{C}$, or a Clifford algebra $\mathrm{Cl}(p,q)$). Suppose one has fixed a notion of $A$-regularity for functions $f:\Omega\subset A^n\to A$, meaning a first-order constant-coefficient linear differential operator $D_A^{(n)}$ (a Cauchy–Fueter type operator) such that the $A$-regular functions of $n$ variables are exactly the solutions of $D_A^{(n)} f=0$.

Problem. Find a hypercomplex algebra $C$ (depending on $A$ and $n$) together with a Cauchy–Fueter–type operator $D_C^{(1)}$ defining a notion of $C$-regularity for functions $g:\Omega'\subset C\to C$ of a single $C$-variable, and an embedding/identification
$$\iota:A^n \hookrightarrow C, \qquad \pi:C\to A,$$
such that every $A$-regular function $f:\Omega\to A$ of $n$ variables arises as $f = \pi\circ g\circ \iota$ for some $C$-regular function $g$ of one $C$-variable, and conversely the pullback of every $C$-regular $g$ yields an $A$-regular $f$.

As motivating instances, one requires that:
(i) when $A=\mathbb{H}$ and $n=2$, the algebra $C$ may be taken to be the biquaternions $\mathbb{H}\otimes_{\mathbb{R}}\mathbb{C}$, with an appropriate one-variable regularity;
(ii) alternatively, $C$ may be taken to be a suitable Clifford algebra, again with a one-variable Cauchy–Fueter–type regularity recovering the two-quaternionic-variable Fueter-regular functions.

Determine such an algebra $C$ and one-variable regularity for general $A$ and $n\ge 2$.
artifact.status_search_result: This is stated as an open research problem in hypercomplex analysis concerning Cauchy–Fueter systems in several variables. No published solution providing a general construction of such an algebra $C$ and one-variable regularity reducing $n$-variable $A$-regularity to one-variable $C$-regularity could be located; only the motivating quaternion/biquaternion/Clifford examples are known.

status_evidence.title: Some open problems on the analysis of the Cauchy-Fueter system in several variables
status_evidence.snippet: Survey listing open problems on Cauchy-Fueter systems; the problem of embedding several-variable regularity into one-variable regularity over a larger hypercomplex algebra is posed as open.
status_evidence.claim: The problem is posed as open with only motivating examples (quaternionic to biquaternionic/Clifford) known.
